question.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $G$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[G\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $G$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $G$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[G\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}.
$$

The matrix ${G}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{G}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{3} & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
